messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a small latency regression on non-chat reranker endpoints after the recent kernel-selection change. Starts around the time we enabled the int8 fast-paths.

maria: Hmm, how small? numbers? can you paste profiling? :thinking_face:

alex: End-to-end p50 +12ms on 64-query batch, p95 +28ms. This is on dedicated pools (r4) with batching enabled. Locally repro with the perf harness.

jon: Did kernel selection fall back to a different GEMM kernel for mid-size sequences? we had a fallback for seq>128 that was a bit slower in fp16->int8 transitions.

alex: Exactly. Profiling shows kernel flip at seq=128 boundary. Quick paste of the perf snippet:
```
Profiling summary (rerank, non-chat)
model: small-ranker-v2
seq_len=64  tokens/s=11.8k  kernel=fast_gemm_fp16  GPU SM util=54%
seq_len=128 tokens/s=6.4k   kernel=int8_gemm_packed  GPU SM util=49%
seq_len=256 tokens/s=3.6k   kernel=int8_gemv_fallback  GPU SM util=35%
KV cache hit-rate ~4% (warm start)
Observed per-request latency bump around kernel boundary: +10..+30ms
```

maria: KV warmup low makes sense for rerank (short lived requests). Two knobs to try: reduce max_token_budget per batch so kernel stays in the fast path, or add smoothing to batch formation so we avoid forming mid-size batches that trigger the fallback.

lisa: We should also consider kernel selection hysteresis — avoid switching kernels for a small shift in seq distribution. Might be cheaper than throttling batching.

jon: Agreed. Hysteresis + token-budget soft-cap seems promising. Proposed changes:
- max_token_budget: 1024 -> 512 for rerank endpoints by default
- soft_cap_ratio: 0.85 (allow small overfill but not full flip)
- smoothing: exp_decay(alpha=0.92) on recent seq histogram for batch formation
```
batch_policy {
  max_token_budget: 512
  soft_cap_ratio: 0.85
  smoothing: exp_decay(0.92)
  prefer_small_batches_for_nonchat: true
}
```

alex: I can run a canary with those settings on a single pool. Would like to keep per-token throughput good while preventing the kernel flip.

maria: Also add a quick metric: kernel_selected and kernel_switch_count per minute, and KV_hit_rate per route. If switch_count spikes after rollout, rollback.

ops-bot: deploy-triggered: canary pool r4-canary created for batch-policy-expt-1854 (owner: alex).

ci-bot: perf-harness job queued -> job id 7892, expect ~30m.

jon: One more idea: make reranker queue policy bias toward forming many small batches (N=8..16 queries) rather than fewer large ones. Rerank requests are cheap per query but heavy on seq because we fetch many candidates. Small batches keep seq_len per sample lower.

lisa: Risk: smaller batches increase per-request scheduling overhead and reduce batching efficiency. We'll need to tune the tradeoff in the canary. Suggest metrics to capture: tokens/sec, latency p50/p95, kernel_switch_count, batch_size_distribution, effective_unit_cost.

alex: Agreed. My plan: run 3 canary variants over next 24h:
- A: max_token_budget=512 + smoothing alpha=0.92
- B: same + small-batch-bias (target batch size 12)
- C: hysteresis only (kernel hysteresis window=10% seq shift)
I will post results in this thread.

maria: Assigning owners: alex runs canaries, jon implements hysteresis PR, lisa adds metrics dashboard, i'll own analysis + decision. Please open PR/issue refs.

alex: opened issue #3421 with experiment plan and linked PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 (batcher changes) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/rust-kernels/pull/1287 (hysteresis guard).

ci-bot: perf job 7892 completed. summary: A (512+smooth) p50 -8ms vs baseline, p95 -4ms, kernel_switch_count -62%. tokens/sec -3% impact.

alex: Canary A looks promising. Lower tokens/sec but net latency improved and kernel switches dropped. Will run B/C next.

maria: Nice. If B keeps latency and brings tokens/sec back up, we can stage a wider rollout to dedicated pools with a config flag per-route. Also add a fallback rule: if kernel_switch_count > 10/min during rollout, auto-revert to previous batch_policy.

jon: I'll land the hysteresis PR with tests today. Adding an opt-in config key `kernel_hysteresis_pct` default 0 (disabled) so we can enable per-customer.

lisa: I'll build dashboard widgets under "Rerank batching experiments" and include batch_size histograms and kernel_switch_rate.

alex: Thanks all — will update after B/C. Keeping thread open for rollout decisions. :thumbsup:
